chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Hammad, from Hareez, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Baseer and Bureyd ibn Muawiya al-Ijaly and Fuzayl ibn Yasaar, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah imposed zakat alongside salat on wealth, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) established it as a sunnah for nine things, and the Messenger of Allah exempted whatever was besides these — in gold, silver, camels, cattle, sheep, wheat, barley, dates, and raisins — and exempted whatever was besides that.

key_terms.الزَّكَاةَ: Zakat — the obligatory alms-tax, one of the five pillars of Islam
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: Salat — ritual prayer, here used to show zakat's equal importance alongside prayer
key_terms.سَنَّهَا: Established as sunnah — the Prophet specified the practical application of the divine command
key_terms.عَفَا: Exempted/pardoned — formal legal exemption from the obligation
key_terms.فَرَضَ: Divinely ordained/imposed — denotes a binding religious obligation (fard)

ai.seo_question: What nine things is zakat obligatory upon according to Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith, reported through multiple highly reliable companions of Imams al-Baqir and al-Sadiq (as), establishes the fundamental legal ruling that zakat is divinely mandated alongside salat as the two cornerstone obligations of Islam. The Prophet (saww) defined the scope of zakat by establishing it specifically for nine categories of wealth — two precious metals, three types of livestock, and four agricultural products — and explicitly exempted all other categories. This delimitation was crucial for early Muslim communities who needed clear legal boundaries to fulfill their religious duties without undue burden.
